subject: rhwrite hangs with an object of 800MB?

messages.author: 0c2bffd1ce4a1edd
messages.subject: rhwrite hangs with an object of 800MB?
parts:

Using rhwripe I tried to upload an object to HDFS.

>n=104857600
>dataset=data.frame(matrix(runif(n,0.0,1),n/2))

> rhwrite(dataset,"/temp/xpto")

# After one week waiting, it did not finished.

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: rhwrite hangs with an object of 800MB?
parts:
A week ehh?  That is persistence.

I wonder if it is on the R front-end side.  rhwrite converts data.frame to a list of rows as key,value pairs  via:
lo <- lapply(1:nrow(lo), function(i) list(rlo[i], lo[i,]))  That is not a particularly inspiring R operation for data.frames with 104 million rows.  Whether or not it is the cause of the problem, I don't know, but I do know there are larger issues to consider and none are ideal for this use-case including this code bit.

rhwrite is about writing list of  key,value pairs.  It allows you some flexibility on input, but key,value pairs of string and doublet numeric record isn't a very good use-case for Hadoop with serialized data in general.

I would take a little more ownership over the use case and design your key,value pairs to be better in general.  If you really like every row number is a key, and every value is row from a data.frame.  The way I would go about it is to design my input to rhwrite to be chunks of the data.frame, and then run a MapReduce job to split them by row.  It should parallelize a lot of the detail work instead of writing out 104 million key,value pairs from the front-end.

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: rhwrite hangs with an object of 800MB?
parts:
Hello,

I guess it went stuck in the R front-end side. I assume this because the server has 6 CPUs and only one was busy with a R process (not a Java VM).
There should be much more efficients ways that my naive and silly approach. Since I want to test some map reduce algorithms using Rhipe I am not concern about the performance of storing the dataset in HDFS. I just want to store it in the simplest way to allow me spend time playing with map reduce.

In reality, I have a csv file with MM of lines, and each line has several values.
Something like:

val-1, val-2, val-3, ..., val-i
val-1, val-2, val-3, ..., val-i
...

My naive and simplistic approach would be:
- to import the .csv file into R
- write the imported R object into HDFS using rhwrite

At the end, I would like to have the data stored in HDFS where the key is the number of the csv's row and the corresponding value would be a list(val-1, val-2, val-3, ..., val-i). 

Of course, this does not make sense as a generic approach. 
It would make more sense to have a tool to directly import the csv to HDFS maintaining the desired struct of an R object.

Any ideas how to easily import csv into HDFS maintaining the mentioned key,val structure?

Thanks,
Rui

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: rhwrite hangs with an object of 800MB?
parts:
How important is the key being the row number? The import can easily
be done in parallel using RHIPE (as a mapreduce job).
But preserving line numbers will be tricky since the file is processed
in parallel.

The lineinputformat which is in RHIPE for processing files at line
level can be used for this (and will require one modification) -
however
the import will be done sequentially - in chunks of lines. It wont
take a week, but wont be parallel. It will preserve line numbers.

If k is a key, what properties should k have?
